newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close modestly lower.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close modestly lower.

text.p: Argentine stocks gave back early gains and drifted gently lower at the close Wednesday as part of a normal pullback, dealers said.

"The bolsa was going too strong and a correction was expected," said Andres McKiguan at Velox traders. "The slide will probably continue ahead of Friday's options expirations and it's good, because many players are waiting on the sidelines for a chance to get back in with lower prices."
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV shed 0.3 percent to close at 729.72. It had halted a seven-session rise Tuesday, when it also lost 0.3 percent.
Traders said the bolsa was also affected by a sharp reversal Wednesday on the Brazilian markets, especially in bellwether stock Telebras.
"People are squaring positions and looking at the behavior of the markets abroad, but it's not a change of trend," another trader said. "Local fundamentals remain excellent."

The dealer noted turnover had recovered to last week's healthy levels, with floor volume reaching 34.8 million pesos Wednesday against 31.2 million Tuesday and 20 million Monday. Over-the-counter deals also picked up to 97.2 million pesos from 61.8 million Tuesday.
The broad market closed off 0.2 percent, with winners outpacing losers 31 to 24 and 18 issues closing flat.

The day's biggest main-tier risers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which rallied 4.8 percent after a long losing spell, and Bansud, which rose 1.1 percent. Telecom, Banco de Galicia and Transportadora de Gas del Sur all tacked on 0.8 percent.
MerVal losers were led by electricity distributor Central Costanera and carmaker Ciadea, both off 1.7 percent, and holding company Perez Companc off 1.3 percent.
